messages.author: 43d8e5920c5b5dac
messages.subject: S_X2 degrees of freedom
parts:
Hi Phil!

I am fitting several dichotomous IRT models to simulated 9-item data with large sample size. When I investigate the fit indices I noticed S_X2 statiatic, its df, p, and RMSEA is NA for some items. Also, S_X2 df is different for the remaining items, even though they are of the same “itemtype”. Could you provide some insights of these two issues? Thank you!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: S_X2 degrees of freedom
parts:
Can you demonstrate this issue first hand with some reproducible code? I imagine this has to do with the extremeness of the generated parameters since the S_X2 is conditional on piece-wises total score statistics. 

Phil

Here's a table of your response counts:

> apply(dat, 2, table)

Have 4/10000 positive endorsements, which is why a partitioned total score method like S_X2 fails when collapsing the response counts. E.g., compare the default which collapses cells with expected values less than 1:

parts:

Phil
